metadata.title: Writing a Structured Abstract
metadata.audience: Students and practitioners learning to use and report on AI systems
metadata.fellow: Janvi Chitroda, AI Data Engineer volunteer, Medhavy project, Humanitarians AI
metadata.source: inbox/term2-week03/term2-week3-video-content.md (Week 3); narration supplied verbatim and pre-approved by Janvi (2026-10-27)
metadata.note: STEM/learning film, hai Plain register on the ai-explainer chassis. Thesis: a structured abstract says what was done and what was found; why each design choice was made belongs in the methods. Cut rationale, never results. Example: Janvi's own JBI abstract (345 → 285 words). Narration supplied verbatim and pre-approved by Janvi (2026-10-27).

beats.role_note: COLD OPEN LAW — Claude composer, ask lands answered. Required intro line + AI-narration disclosure.
beats.narration_text: Hi, I am Janvi and this video is about writing a structured abstract, using the one I wrote for our journal submission. This narration is an AI-generated voice; the work is mine.

props.command: My structured abstract is 345 words and the limit is 300. What do I cut?
output: Keep what you did and what you found
Move the why to the methods

beats.role_note: Five labelled boxes (Objective · Materials and Methods · Results · Discussion · Conclusion) light on each spoken name; bracket '300 words total'.
beats.narration_text: A structured abstract splits into labelled parts, and each part has one job. The Journal of Biomedical Informatics requires five: Objective, Materials and Methods, Results, Discussion, and Conclusion. All five must fit in 300 words.
beats.visual_intent: Five labelled boxes (Objective · Materials and Methods · Results · Discussion · Conclusion) light on each spoken name; bracket '300 words total'.

beats.role_note: Items to fit: two phases (generation → review) · 10,049 → 8,053 keywords · 927 → 915 acronyms · 5 tags · 3 models; counter 'first draft: 345 words' past a 300 line.
beats.narration_text: Mine had to hold a two-phase pipeline, generation and review, plus the numbers: 10,049 keywords down to 8,053, 927 acronyms down to 915, five tags and three models. My first draft was 345 words.
beats.visual_intent: Items to fit: two phases (generation → review) · 10,049 → 8,053 keywords · 927 → 915 acronyms · 5 tags · 3 models; counter 'first draft: 345 words' past a 300 line.

beats.role_note: Rule card: WHAT you did + WHAT you found → abstract; WHY → methods.
beats.narration_text: The rule I used: the abstract says what was done and what was found. Why you made each design choice belongs in the methods section.
beats.visual_intent: Rule card: WHAT you did + WHAT you found → abstract; WHY → methods.

show.event: what you did + what you found → abstract

beats.role_note: Long-sentence block (three models · providers · why mixed) struck; 'a three-model cross-provider ensemble' highlighted; '~25 words → 4'.
beats.narration_text: One example. I had a full sentence naming all three models, their providers, and why I mixed providers, about 25 words. I cut it to a few: a three-model cross-provider ensemble.
beats.visual_intent: Long-sentence block (three models · providers · why mixed) struck; 'a three-model cross-provider ensemble' highlighted; '~25 words → 4'.

show.event: full sentence: models · providers · why mixed (~25 words)

beats.role_note: Word bar with a 300 limit line; counter 345 → 285.
beats.narration_text: Cuts like that took the abstract from 345 words to 285, under the limit.
beats.visual_intent: Word bar with a 300 limit line; counter 345 → 285.

beats.role_note: Chips: 'findings' and 'numbers' marked keep (teal tick); 'rationale' marked cut (struck); line 'abstract only → still know what you did and what you got'.
beats.narration_text: What not to cut: the findings and the numbers behind them. A reader who sees only the abstract should still know what you did and what you got. If a cut removes a result, put it back and cut rationale instead.
beats.visual_intent: Chips: 'findings' and 'numbers' marked keep (teal tick); 'rationale' marked cut (struck); line 'abstract only → still know what you did and what you got'.

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW — suggested prompt typed in the composer.
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Take your abstract and label each sentence as did, found, or why. Move every why sentence to your methods, then count the words you saved.

props.command: Label each sentence of my abstract as DID, FOUND or WHY, and suggest which WHY sentences to move to methods.

beats.narration_text: Writing a Structured Abstract. Humanitarians AI.
